event_description: The world finished loading enough to stand on, with how long it took and how much was drawn.
The visitor moved for the first time, choosing to be in the world rather than look at it.
A visitor or an agent added something to the world, which is the act the whole design exists to enable.
Something was taken back out of the world.
The relay declined a build and said why, which is how quota and validation friction becomes visible.
A visitor walked up to something and read it.
The world became shared, with the measured clock offset and how long the connection took.
The world degraded to solo play, which is designed behaviour and needs to be distinguishable from a bug.
One reading of frame rate, draw calls and chunk count per session, so slow devices are visible without sampling every frame.
